transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (CTO, OptiRetail), Leah Kim (Head of Platform), Miguel Torres (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
- Deep dive on Dedicated vs Hosted for high-throughput inference for OptiRetail fraud/rec text use cases.
- Discussed latency SLOs, throughput guarantees, noisy neighbor mitigation, KV cache behavior, batching strategies, and quantization trade-offs.
- Agreed next steps: pricing deck, SOC2/ISO docs, pilot benchmark on dedicated cluster, and sample KV/batching config.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off in a sec, I'm Ava from Redwood, and Ravi's our systems SE.
[00:14] Samir Rao: Hey thanks, Samir here. We're excited to understand the dedicated offering; our main drivers are predictable throughput and isolation — noisy neighbor has bitten us on other clouds.
[00:29] Ravi Patel: Great, quick agenda: architecture differences, perf characteristics (latency/throughput), caching and batching, quantization options, and VPC/on-prem considerations, then Q&A.
[00:45] Leah Kim: Sounds good. We have a pretty bursty load — marketing campaigns spike qps by 6-8x for short windows. Cost is important but predictability is bigger.
[00:58] Miguel Torres: Also our security team needs audit logs and KMS integration for keys.
[01:12] Ava Martinez: Noted. I'll start high-level: hosted gives you lowest-friction onboarding and automatic scaling, but it's multi-tenant — we do SLOs but no hard per-customer throughput guarantees like Dedicated. Dedicated is reserved pools with tenant isolation, predictable throughput, and can be in your VPC for private deployments.
[01:33] Samir Rao: When you say "reserved pools" — how isolated is that at the GPU level? Can we see noisy neighbor cross-talk?
[01:46] Ravi Patel: Good question. For Dedicated we allocate dedicated GPU nodes to your tenancy. There's minimal interference; network buffers and device context are isolated. We still run a shared control plane unless you pick Private. The main noisy neighbor vector is host-level contention — we pin CUDA contexts and cgroups to mitigate it. In practice customers see much tighter p95/p99 stability.
[02:12] Leah Kim: Any documented numbers?
[02:16] Ravi Patel: We have benchmark sheets — I'll share the spreadsheet link after the call. Example: for a Llama-2-13b style model, hosted median latency 120ms, p95 260ms during spikes; Dedicated median 115ms, p95 140ms under similar load with proper batching. Those are tuned figures — actual depends on sequence length and batch policy.
[02:40] Miguel Torres: Sequence lengths vary a lot for us, average 64 tokens but tail to 512 for some sessions. How does KV cache factor in?
[02:50] Ravi Patel: KV cache reduces recomputation for streaming contexts. On Dedicated you can size KV backing store for lower eviction rates; on Hosted we share cache memory policies across tenants so eviction can be higher during heavy global load. For long sessions, Dedicated gives more predictable cache hit rates.
[03:12] Samir Rao: Are there examples of eviction impacting latency?
[03:17] Ravi Patel: Yes — if KV cache evicts, tokens need to be recomputed and that adds 50-200ms depending on model and position. We also have prefix caching for common prompts which helps.
[03:33] Ava Martinez: Also worth noting we support both prefix/KV caching and a managed content cache layer that sits in front of the runtime. For Dedicated pilots we can tune cache sizes.
[03:46] Leah Kim: Batching — we see spikes. How do you balance batching vs tail latency?
[03:52] Ravi Patel: Continuous batching aggregates requests to improve throughput and lower cost, but it increases tail latency if you wait too long. On Dedicated you can configure latency SLO-driven batching windows and set max batch sizes; we also do adaptive thresholds based on observed qps. For ultra-low p95 you run smaller max batch sizes and prefer more nodes. There's a tradeoff: cost per token goes up as you reduce batching efficiency.
[04:18] Miguel Torres: Any auto-burst for short spikes?
[04:21] Ava Martinez: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale policies to add more nodes temporarily; you commit baseline capacity and can allow burst to cloud spare capacity. There's a cost delta but it helps handle marketing bursts.
[04:34] Samir Rao: Quantization — we have mixed workloads, some require FP16 outputs. How do you handle int8/int4 and latency differences?
[04:42] Ravi Patel: We provide quantized model variants. int8 gives big speedups and memory savings; int4 more aggressive but can affect quality. On Dedicated you can deploy specific quantized binaries for your cluster. Hosted offers quantized variants too but may route to compatible hardware broadly. Quantization reduces per-token latency and memory pressure, which also helps with KV capacity.
[05:05] Leah Kim: Do you support dynamic quantization or pruning in-flight?
[05:09] Ravi Patel: Not dynamic at inference time; we publish pre-quantized artifacts and recommended QA steps. For experiments we can do custom quant builds in pilot with our applied-ML team.
[05:20] Samir Rao: Network and VPC concerns: we need private networking and egress controls. Can Dedicated be in our VPC?
[05:28] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC with Private control plane options; for strict regulatory needs we offer Private (on-prem) deployments. We'll need a network checklist — we'll share it (Ravi).
[05:41] Miguel Torres: Is SSO and SAML available for Dedicated?
[05:44] Ravi Patel: Yes, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has SSO too but some enterprise features like BYOK require Dedicated/Private.
[05:59] Leah Kim: How do you handle software updates and kernel changes on Dedicated? We can't afford runtime drift during peak seasons.
[06:07] Ravi Patel: We manage runtime updates via scheduled maintenance windows; you control rollout policies — canary, A/B, or pinned patches. For Dedicated you can pin runtime versions and delay non-critical updates. We try to avoid kernel-level changes during pilots unless critical.
[06:25] Samir Rao: Can you explain throughput guarantees more concretely? We want a contract that guarantees X qps at Y p95.
[06:34] Ava Martinez: For Dedicated we offer commit tiers — you reserve a baseline of slots (GPU capacity) and we guarantee throughput within that baseline. For example, a committed 20-GPU cluster for your model topology maps to a measurable sustained qps at your target token length; the SLA will reflect uptime and a best-effort p95 target. Hard p95 guarantees are tricky because of model variance and network factors, but we can define commercial SLA terms with financial remedies.
[06:58] Miguel Torres: So the SLA is mostly uptime + capacity, and p95 is an objective that we measure in the pilot?
[07:04] Ava Martinez: Exactly — p95 and p99 are measured during onboarding and the pilot. Based on that we size the commit.
[07:12] Leah Kim: Any noisy neighbor scenarios on Dedicated we should still watch for?
[07:16] Ravi Patel: Possibly on shared storage or control-plane bursts; but we isolate GPU scheduling. We also enforce IO QoS on NVMe-backed instances. We'll instrument and surface noisy neighbor anomalies in the Console.
[07:30] Samir Rao: About cost — can you give a rough unit comparison hosted vs dedicated for sustained workloads?
[07:36] Ava Martinez: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing; Dedicated has committed monthly cost but lower per-token variable cost. For sustained high-throughput, Dedicated is typically 30-50% cheaper on unit economics. We'll send a model showing TCO given your qps/seq len.
[07:53] Miguel Torres: For the pilot, what's the minimal footprint to test KV behavior and batching?
[07:58] Ravi Patel: We usually start with 4 GPUs for a mid-sized model to observe cache hit rates and batching efficiency, then scale to 8-16 for production. That's what we recommend for your traffic pattern.
[08:12] Leah Kim: Any caveats for on-prem? Our infra team is worried about GPU driver versions and kernel compat.
[08:19] Ravi Patel: Our on-prem package lists exact driver/kernel versions; we provide an ops checklist and try to keep the surface small. For air-gapped we ship certified images. Note: on-prem support has an ops surcharge and longer lead times.
[08:36] Samir Rao: Can you walk through a sample timeline for pilot -> production?
[08:40] Ava Martinez: Typical: week 0 — pilot scoping + infra prep; week 1-2 — deploy pilot and run benchmarks; week 3 — analyze results and tuning; week 4-6 — production cutover and provision committed capacity. We can compress with more engineering support.
[09:00] Miguel Torres: Ok. On benchmarking, can you run a 95th percentile test that includes our long-tail sequences (512 tokens)?
[09:07] Ravi Patel: Yes — we can run synthetic and real traffic replays. For long tails we'll measure cold-cache vs warmed KV cache. Expect p95 difference of several hundred ms on cold cache; with warmed cache it tightens.
[09:25] Leah Kim: What about model updates — if we roll a new model version frequently, does Dedicated help or hurt?
[09:31] Ravi Patel: Dedicated helps because you control rollout windows and can pin capacity; but rolling new model binaries requires model warmup and caching warm phases. We recommend blue/green deploys for model swaps to avoid cache thrash.
[09:47] Samir Rao: Any customers with similar scale you can reference? (high-level)
[09:51] Ava Martinez: We have retail and ads customers with similar spikes; we'll send anonymized case study links.
[09:59] Miguel Torres: OK thanks. A few quick clarifications: 1) Is KV cache persisted across restarts? 2) Does Dedicated let us use custom quant builds? 3) Can we get network egress filtering?
[10:12] Ravi Patel: 1) KV cache is in-memory; we have managed persistence patterns for session stores but not full persistent KV across hard restarts unless you run Private with customer-managed storage. 2) Yes for Dedicated/Private we can load custom quant artifacts in the cluster. 3) Yes, VPC peering and egress ACLs supported, network checklist will have details.
[10:34] Leah Kim: On monitoring — how granular are logs and traces? Our compliance needs per-token cost breakdowns sometimes.
[10:42] Ava Martinez: Console has per-route and token-level cost breakdown, traces for requests, and audit logs. For Dedicated you get longer retention options as an add-on.
[10:56] Samir Rao: Any gotchas around multi-region replication for failover?
[11:00] Ravi Patel: Cross-region replication is supported but increases KV warming complexity; we often recommend active-passive with regional caches warmed on failover.
[11:12] Miguel Torres: Alright. Let's recap and make sure we captured next steps.
[11:18] Ava Martinez: Recap: we'll send dedicated pricing and SOW, SOC2/ISO + network checklist, a pilot plan for week of 3/30 with 4-8 GPU footprint to measure KV cache and batching, and Ravi will run initial perf tests and share spreadsheet. Customer to confirm target p95 and share internal traces.
[11:40] Samir Rao: That matches. We'll aim to get you our traces by Friday.
[11:44] Leah Kim: Please include the case studies and the sample config for KV cache/batching.
[11:48] Ava Martinez: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[11:52] Miguel Torres: Thanks.
